Motivated by the lack of vsini and stellar parameter measurements for most of the known HVSs and the possibility of testing the nature of the SMBH in the center of our Galaxy, we performed high resolution spectroscopy of two HVSs.

values.condition: Heliocentric radial velocity; previous work (Brown et al. 2007), who report two observations with identical values within their errorbars

notes: Both HVS7 and HVS8 are follow_up targets: the paper describes them as two of the ten already known HVSs (T:p1-b6, T:p7-b1) and studies them spectroscopically as known HVSs (T:p2-b3). HVS7 is not a newly established candidate because the authors note that its radial velocity is marginally consistent with a bound BHB runaway and that astrometry is needed (T:p6-b2); follow_up applies regardless of that current boundness ambiguity. For HVS8, the coordinate alias at T:p2-b5 is printed as J094214.04+200322.1 without a repeated SDSS prefix, so only that supplied form is recorded.
HVS8: HVS8 is identified as SDSS J094214.04+200322.1 in T:p2-b5, but the paper does not separately report right ascension or declination values.
